name: Impact Attempt – Destructive or Disruptive Actions on Linux Hosts
description: This rule detects potentially destructive actions that may result in system instability, data loss, or disruption of operations. Such impact-focused behavior often occurs in the final stages of an attack, where the adversary attempts to break system functionality, delete critical files, wipe devices, or stop essential services like logging or security monitoring.
note:
- Identify the user and process context of the destructive command.
- Determine whether the action was intentional (e.g., system maintenance) or malicious.
- Check for previous stages of the attack (e.g., initial access, privilege escalation).
- Review logs to assess damage or files deleted or overwritten.
query:
event.module: "auditd" and
auditd.log.record_type: "EXECVE" and
(
  (
    process.executable: "rm" and
    (
      process.args: "/etc/passwd" or
      process.args: "/etc/shadow" or
      process.args: "/home/*/.bash_history" or
      process.args: "/var/log/auth.log" or
      process.args: "/var/log/secure"
    )
  )
  or
  (
    process.executable: "shred" and
    (
      process.args: "/etc/passwd" or
      process.args: "/etc/shadow"
    )
  )
  or
  (
    process.executable: "dd" and
    (
      process.args: "/etc/shadow" or
      process.args: "/etc/passwd"
    )
  )
  or
  (
    process.executable: "systemctl" and
    (
      process.args: "*stop*" or
      process.args: "*disable*"
    ) and
    (
      process.args: "*rsyslog*" or
      process.args: "*systemd-journald*" or
      process.args: "*auditd*"
    )
  )
  or
  (
    process.executable: "shutdown" or
    process.executable: "reboot"
  )
)
and not user.name: "clamav"
and not process.args: "*clamscan*"
